- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2 days above peak or apply decay factor.
- If sentiment is negative (0.0) and prices are trending down, model underestimates; add 1–3% buffer to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model consistently underestimates in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days) — apply upward bias of 1–2% for first 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows multiple 1.0 spikes, model overreacts; dampen forecast by 5–10% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >15% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 2–5% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum — add 1–3% upward adjustment for last 5–7 days if sentiment is positive.
